# Brandywine Fisheries
> Oregon coast seafood from a local fishing family. Never-frozen Oregon seafood from a hand-built boat working out of Charleston harbor. Retail store in Springfield, Oregon plus five farmers market days a week.

## Facts
- Store: 4731 Main St #1, Springfield, OR 97478 — open Open Daily 10am – 6pm
- Phone: (541) 505-9686
- Home port: Charleston, Oregon
- The boat: 35-year fishing history on the Oregon coast, hand-built in Charleston, one of the core independent boats in that harbor
- Handling: an ICE fish-hold, never frozen — which means the boat docks more often
- Owner: has fished this specific boat for 16 years; lives up the McKenzie River, as does the staff

## Market days
- Eugene: Saturdays, 9am – 3pm — Park Blocks at 8th & Oak St., Eugene, OR
- Eugene: Tuesdays, 10am – 3pm — Park Blocks at 8th & Oak St., Eugene, OR
- Corvallis: Saturdays, 9am – 1pm — 1st & Jackson St., Corvallis, OR
- Bend: Wednesdays, 11am – 3pm — Brooks Alley Way, downtown Bend, between Franklin and Brooks Street
- Portland: Saturdays, 8:30am – 2pm — SW Park and Montgomery, Portland, OR

## Species and prices
- [Chinook Salmon](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/chinook-salmon/): $29.95 / lb. Rich and buttery, the most pronounced salmon flavor of the group. Cook to 125°F for medium-rare in the center. Oregon fishery — Troll.
- [Coho Salmon](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/coho-salmon/): $18.95 / lb. Clean and distinctly salmon, without chinook's heaviness. Cook to 125–130°F in the center. Oregon fishery — Troll.
- [Steelhead](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/steelhead/): Smoked, $40.00. Milder and sweeter than salmon — the reason it takes smoke so well. Cook to 125–130°F if you are cooking a fresh piece. Oregon fishery — Sold by Brandywine primarily in the smokehouse line.
- [Pacific Halibut](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/pacific-halibut/): $38.95 / lb. Clean and mild with a faint sweetness. Cook to 130–135°F. Oregon fishery — Longline.
- [Black Cod (Sablefish)](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/black-cod/): $18.95 / lb. Rich and buttery, closer to a fatty salmon than to a white fish. Cook to 140°F — this is the one fish that genuinely wants to go a little further. Oregon fishery — Longline and pot gear, fished deep.
- [Lingcod](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/lingcod/): $18.95 / lb. Mild and slightly sweet. Cook to 135°F. Oregon fishery — Hook and line, jigged over rocky nearshore ground.
- [Pacific Rockfish](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/pacific-rockfish/): $13.95 / lb. Mild and clean — the least assertive fish in the case. Cook to 135°F. Oregon fishery — Hook and line over nearshore reef.
- [Pacific Cod](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/pacific-cod/): Ask at the counter — availability varies. Mild, clean, faintly sweet. Cook to 135°F. Oregon fishery — Hook and line and trawl gear.
- [Sole and Flounder](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/petrale-sole/): Ask at the counter — availability varies. Delicate and sweet. Cook to 135°F. Oregon fishery — Trawl gear on soft bottom.
- [Albacore Tuna](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/albacore-tuna/): Canned from $12.00; smoked loin $40.00 / lb, $20.00 / half lb. Mild for a tuna, clean, without the iron note of the red tunas. Cook to Sear the outside and leave the middle rare — 115–120°F in the center. Oregon fishery — Troll and jig gear.
- [Ahi (Yellowfin) Tuna](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/ahi-tuna/): $8.95. Clean and mild, with more of a tuna edge than albacore. Cook to Rare — 115°F in the center, or served raw. Sourced, not an Oregon fishery.
- [Swordfish](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/swordfish/): $18.95 (steaks). Mild and slightly sweet, meatier than any other fish in the case. Cook to 130–135°F. Sourced, not an Oregon fishery.
- [Mahi Mahi](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/mahi-mahi/): $9.95. Mild and sweet. Cook to 135°F. Sourced, not an Oregon fishery.
- [Dungeness Crab](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/dungeness-crab/): Ask at the counter — seasonal. Sweet and briny — Oregon's signature shellfish. Cook to Boiled or steamed until hot through. Oregon fishery — Baited pots set on sand and mud bottom.
- [Bay Shrimp](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/bay-shrimp/): $9.00. Sweet and mild. Cook to Already cooked when sold — no further cooking needed. Oregon fishery — Trawl gear fitted with excluder devices.
- [Raw Shrimp](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/raw-shrimp/): 13/15 count $19.95 · 16/20 count $14.95. Sweet and clean. Cook to Cook just until opaque and curled into a loose C. Sourced, not an Oregon fishery.
- [Fresh Oysters](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/pacific-oysters/): Ask at the counter. Briny, cucumber-sweet, with a mineral finish that changes by growing bay. Cook to Raw on the half shell, or grilled just until the shells pop open. Oregon fishery — Farmed on Oregon's estuaries and bays.
- [Black Mussels](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/black-mussels/): $6.95. Sweet and briny. Cook to Steam just until the shells open, three to five minutes. Oregon fishery — Rope-grown.
- [Steamer Clams](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/steamer-clams/): $8.95 — in garlic butter, prepared. Sweet and strongly briny. Cook to Steam until the shells open, five minutes or so. Oregon fishery — Harvested from Oregon's tideflats and bays.
- [Scallops](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/fish/scallops/): Smoked, $20.00. Sweet and rich. Cook to Sear hard and fast — the center should stay just translucent. Sourced, not an Oregon fishery.

## Cooking methods
- [How to grill fish](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/guides/how-to-grill-fish/): Direct high heat over open flame, best on firm fish thick enough to survive being turned.
- [How to pan-sear fish](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/guides/how-to-pan-sear-fish/): A hot heavy pan and very little movement — the most reliable way to cook nearly anything in the case.
- [How to roast fish](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/guides/how-to-roast-fish/): Dry oven heat — the least demanding method and the easiest one to walk away from.
- [How to smok fish](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/guides/how-to-smoke-fish/): Low heat and wood smoke over hours — a preservation method that turned into a delicacy.
- [How to poach fish](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/guides/how-to-poach-fish/): Gentle submersion in barely-moving liquid — the most controlled and least forgiving-of-neglect method.
- [How to fry fish](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/guides/how-to-fry-fish/): Hot oil and a coating — the treatment most of the lean white fish in the case eventually gets.
- [How to serving raw fish](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/guides/how-to-raw-fish/): Crudo, sashimi, ceviche and poke — where handling quality is the entire dish.
- [How to steam fish](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/guides/how-to-steam-fish/): Moist heat in a covered pot — the method shellfish is built for.

## Seasons
- [January](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/season/january/): Crab weather. The quietest month at the markets and one of the best at the counter.
- [February](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/season/february/): Deep winter. Crab, groundfish, and the shortest market list of the year.
- [March](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/season/march/): The turn. Halibut season typically opens and the year starts moving.
- [April](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/season/april/): Pink shrimp season opens and the Corvallis market comes back.
- [May](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/season/may/): Salmon openings begin. The busiest stretch of the year starts here.
- [June](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/season/june/): Full swing. Salmon, halibut, shrimp, and every market open.
- [July](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/season/july/): Albacore arrive off the coast. Peak season, peak markets.
- [August](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/season/august/): Coho month. The crab season closes mid-month.
- [September](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/season/september/): The best month to buy. Salmon, albacore and shrimp all at once.
- [October](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/season/october/): The season winds down. Shrimp closes, the markets start folding.
- [November](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/season/november/): Groundfish takes over and the coast waits on the crab tests.
- [December](https://bannisterderik-tech.github.io/brandywine-fisheries/season/december/): Crab season opens — on paper December 1, in practice usually later.

## Notes on accuracy
- Commercial fishery seasons are set annually and shift year to year. All season information is typical, not guaranteed.
- Prices are Brandywine's published prices and change.
- Species not landed by the Oregon boat (ahi, swordfish, mahi mahi, large raw shrimp, scallops) are labelled as sourced on every page.
- This site carries no reviews or testimonials, and no photographs of the business, its crew, its boat or its work.
